story_thesis: Microsoft expects holiday growth in Xbox games and services even as hardware revenue falls. Game Pass and third-party spending will help show whether a rebound can last.
duplicate_checks: Prior series META LLY AAPL GOOGL AMZN. MSFT unfeatured. No 7 November series ledger, Mag 7 article or matching remote branch. Checked actual current content, topic index, inventories, finance catalogue, morning CI/COP/ZBRA, Irish coverage, and open PRs 43/57/88. Exit offer story mentions content decline once. Other MSFT stories concern AI spending, capacity or Azure.
evidence_table: 10-Q and press release corroborate comparable Xbox revenue of 5379m and 5508m, company revenue of 92279m and 77673m. Recast prior-year data. Difference 129m. Share calculations 5.8% and 7.1%. Flat-Xbox sensitivity 129/77673*100=0.166 percentage points.

10-Q attributes hardware decline of 14% to lower console volumes. Revenue growth is distinct from unit growth. Content/services down 2% reported and 1% constant currency. Third party and Game Pass down, first party up. No dollars allocated by rounded rates.

Call separates Q1 actuals from Q2 outlook of mid to high single digit content/services growth and hardware revenue decline. Slower growth expected in Q3/Q4. Segment profit includes other product groups. Interpretive tests conditional.
